concept_card.statement: Overlapping waves add displacements, then pass on unchanged; close frequencies beat at |f1 − f2|.
concept_card.analogy: Like two queues crossing at a railway gate: they mix briefly, then walk on.
steps: Add displacements point by point while waves overlap.
Afterwards each wave keeps its shape and direction.
A flat string is still moving: energy is kinetic, not lost.
Beat rate = |f1 − f2|; heard pitch ≈ (f1 + f2)/2.
Fixed string: nodes λ/2 apart, fundamental = v/2L.
concept_card.worked_example: Forks 256 Hz, 260 Hz: 4 beats per second, pitch ≈ 258 Hz.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: When the two pulses cancel, they destroy each other and the energy is gone.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: The rope looks completely flat, so it seems nothing is left.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: Flat is not still. At that instant every bit of the rope is moving fast, so all the energy is kinetic. A moment later both pulses reappear.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: Cancellation is only momentary; the energy stays in the rope as motion and both pulses carry on.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: The two pulses hit each other and bounce back like balls.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: Things we see colliding, like cricket balls or marbles, bounce off each other.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: A pulse is not an object; it is a shape moving along the rope. Where two meet, displacements simply add. Send a tall and a short pulse: the tall one ends up at the far end.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: Pulses pass through each other and come out unchanged.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: Beat frequency is f1 + f2, because both sounds play together.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: Superposition means adding, so adding the frequencies feels natural.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: We add displacements, not frequencies. Loudness swells when the waves fall into step and fades when they fall out of step, which happens |f1 − f2| times per second. 440 Hz and 444 Hz give 4 beats, not 884.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: The beat frequency is the average of the two frequencies.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: You really do hear a note near the average, so that number seems like the answer.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: The average, (f1 + f2)/2, is the pitch you hear. The beat is how often the loudness throbs, which is the difference. 506 Hz and 512 Hz: pitch about 509 Hz, beats 6 per second.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: The average is the pitch; the beat rate is |f1 − f2|.

contrast_probes.probe: Two equal and opposite pulses meet in the middle of a rope. A second later, is there any pulse near the ends?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: No, nothing is left, the rope just stays flat.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Yes, each pulse is back near the end it started from.

contrast_probes.probe: Forks of 300 Hz and 304 Hz sound together. What happens to the loudness, and how often?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: It keeps fading away because the waves cancel and the sound energy gets used up.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: It throbs about 604 times a second.

contrast_probes.probe: Forks of 300 Hz and 304 Hz sound together. What happens to the loudness, and how often?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: It keeps fading away because the waves cancel and the sound energy gets used up.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: It throbs about 302 times a second.

contrast_probes.probe: Forks of 300 Hz and 304 Hz face each other across a room. Where their sound waves meet in the middle, what happens?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: The waves bounce off each other and head back toward their own forks.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: You hear a throb about 604 times a second.

contrast_probes.reply_if_first: The waves bounce off each other and head back toward their own forks.

contrast_probes.probe: Forks of 300 Hz and 304 Hz sound together. Roughly how many throbs per second do you hear?
At the instant two opposite pulses make the rope look flat, is the middle of the rope moving or still?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: Still, the pulses have cancelled so nothing is happening there.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Moving fast, the energy is in its motion and the pulses come back out.

contrast_probes.probe: Kabir sends a tall pulse and Meera a short one toward each other on a slinky. After they meet, which pulse reaches Meera's end?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: The short one, it bounces back to her.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: The tall one, it passes straight through.

contrast_probes.probe: Forks of 300 Hz and 304 Hz sound together. Roughly how many throbs per second do you hear?
Forks of 300 Hz and 304 Hz sound together. Which number gives the pitch you hear, and which gives how often it throbs?
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Pitch about 302 Hz, throbbing 4 times a second.
